verifier_reason: test_outputs.py::test_workbench_ui_present: The test failed in the call phase due to an assertion error

items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The visible code is readable: ids such as 'btn-submit-aftersale' and 'modal-danger-confirm' say what they are, and the handlers are grouped under numbered comments ('// 7. After-Sale Submit'). But most of the 3,600 lines were not shown, and the business logic sits in one huge IIFE with few comments.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: A single new file of 3,622 lines, so at most accept. All the event wiring lives in one large DOMContentLoaded callback, and a global mutable `dangerCallback` is shared between handlers. UI handlers call the shopTestAPI methods rather than repeating the logic, which is good.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: The confirm button guards against double clicks ('if (confirmBtn.disabled) return'), import errors are shown to the user, and the API returns ok:false on failure. But after-sale quantities fall back to `parseInt(inp ? inp.value : '1')`, and the hidden tests for rejecting out-of-stock and over-stock cart actions failed.

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: There is a danger-confirm modal, used for reset. Submitting an after-sale refund and submitting an import both call the API directly with no separate confirmation step. The hidden test_workbench_ui_present failed, so the UI is missing something the brief expected.

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: UI handlers call shopTestAPI.checkout, requestAfterSale and importData, so the UI and the test API share one implementation. Integer-cent arithmetic could not be confirmed from the visible code. The final message describes stats as aggregated live from records, and import as validated without overwriting existing data.
